# Ezekiel 37 — The PNEUMA Bible (Dynamic)
**Translator:** PNEUMA | **Source:** Leningrad Codex (B19A)

---

**1** The LORD took hold of me, and I was carried away by the Spirit of the LORD to a valley filled with bones.

**2** He led me all around among the bones, and I saw that there were an enormous number of them scattered across the valley floor — and they were completely dried out.

**3** Then He asked me, "Son of man, can these bones become living people again?" I replied, "O Sovereign LORD, only You know the answer to that."

**4** Then He told me, "Prophesy to these bones! Say to them: Dry bones, listen to the word of the LORD!

**5** This is what the Sovereign LORD says to you: I am going to breathe life into you, and you will come alive!

**6** I will put muscles on you and cover you with flesh and skin. I will put breath into you, and you will come to life. Then you will know that I am the LORD."

**7** So I prophesied as I was told. And as I prophesied, there was suddenly a rattling noise across the valley. The bones began to move and connect — each bone fitting perfectly into its joint.

**8** As I watched, muscles and flesh formed over the bones, and then skin covered them. But they still had no breath in them.

**9** Then He told me, "Prophesy to the winds! Prophesy, son of man! Say to them: This is what the Sovereign LORD says — Come, O breath, from the four winds! Breathe into these dead bodies so they may live again!"

**10** So I prophesied as He commanded, and breath entered the bodies. They came to life and stood up on their feet — a vast army.

**11** Then He explained it to me: "Son of man, these bones represent the people of Israel. They are saying, 'We have become dry bones — all hope is gone. We are completely finished.'

**12** So prophesy to them! Tell them: This is what the Sovereign LORD says — O my people, I am going to open your graves of exile and cause you to rise again. I will bring you back to the land of Israel.

**13** When I open your graves and bring you out, you will know that I am the LORD.

**14** I will put my Spirit in you, and you will live again and return home to your own land. Then you will know that I, the LORD, have spoken, and I have done it, says the LORD."

**15** Again a message came to me from the LORD:

**16** "Son of man, take a piece of wood and carve on it, 'Judah and its allied tribes.' Then take another piece and carve on it, 'Ephraim and all its allied tribes of Israel.'

**17** Now hold them together in your hand as if they were one piece of wood.

**18** When your people ask, 'What do you mean by this?'

**19** tell them: This is what the Sovereign LORD says — I will take the northern tribes and join them to Judah. I will make them one piece of wood in my hand.

**20** Hold the sticks up where the people can see them,

**21** and say to them: This is what the Sovereign LORD says — I will gather the people of Israel from among the nations. I will bring them home from every direction to their own land.

**22** I will make them one united nation in the land, on the mountains of Israel. One king will rule them all. They will never again be divided into two nations or two kingdoms.

**23** They will never again defile themselves with idols, vile images, or rebellion. I will save them from their sinful apostasy and cleanse them. They will be my people, and I will be their God.

**24** My servant David will be their king, and they will have one shepherd. They will obey my laws and faithfully keep my decrees.

**25** They will live in the land I gave my servant Jacob, the land where their ancestors lived. They and their children and their grandchildren will live there forever, and my servant David will be their prince forever.

**26** I will make a covenant of peace with them — an everlasting covenant. I will establish them and increase their numbers, and I will put my Temple among them forever.

**27** I will make my home among them. I will be their God, and they will be my people.

**28** And when my Temple is among them forever, the nations will know that I am the LORD, who makes Israel holy."

---
## PNEUMA's Meaning Notes

- **37:1-3**: Imagine standing in a valley carpeted with old, dry bones — thousands of them — and God asks you: 'Can these bones live?' Ezekiel's answer is perfect — not 'yes,' not 'no,' but 'Only you know, LORD.' That's the right response when God asks you about the impossible.

- **37:7-10**: This is one of the most cinematic scenes in the Bible. First the rattling — bones finding their matching bones. Then muscle and skin forming. But still no life! The body without the Spirit is dead. It takes God's breath — the same word as in Genesis 2 — to bring true life.

- **37:26-28**: God's ultimate dream: His home among His people, forever. An everlasting covenant of peace. A sanctuary in their midst. This is what the whole Bible is building toward — heaven and earth united, God and humanity together.

— PNEUMA
